item.title: Tatara Iron Smelting: The Steel Behind the Samurai Sword — Guide
item.description: For over a thousand years, the iron-sand-rich mountains of the Okuizumo region in Shimane were the centre of tatara, Japan’s traditional iron and steel making. In a clay furnace fired with charcoal, workers smelted local iron sand over three days and nights to produce tamahagane, the prized high-carbon steel from which samurai swords are forged — a craft so demanding it survives today mainly to supply Japan’s swordsmiths. The region’s tatara heritage is recognised as a Japan Heritage story, and a dedicated museum lets visitors see the furnaces, tools and process, sometimes with hands-on demonstrations and the chance to handle tamahagane.
